The long 2θ scan (Figure 1a) of the as-deposited film (53 nm) shows preferentially oriented diffraction peak at 2θ ≈ 20.21° corresponds to the (001) plane of an orthorhombic phase of V2O5 (Pmmn space group, JCPDS card No. 9-387) along with planes of c-sapphire. XRD pattern of the post-deposition annealed film (Figure 1b) shows rhombohedral V2O3 phase having R-3c space group (JCPDS card no. 26-278), with preferred orientation of (006) plane at 2θ ≈ 38.64° and (0012) plane at ≈ 82.81° along with planes of c-sapphire. The V2O5 and V2O3 films’ thicknesses were examined using cross-sectional field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) images ( Figure 2 ). The average thicknesses of V2O5 and V2O3 thin films of 1000 ALD cycles are 53 and 48 nm, respectively (Figure 2a,b). Figure 3 a,b shows the in-plane FESEM images of V2O5 (53 nm) and V2O3 (48 nm) films, which exhibit the morphology of the grains of the films. Figure 3c,d shows the 3D-view atomic force microscopy (AFM) images of V2O5 (53 nm) and V2O3 (48 nm) films exhibit the typical roughness. Raman spectroscopy plays a significant role in investigating the phases and structures of the materials. In the X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), the binding energy difference (Δ) between the O1s and the V2p3/2 can be used to identify the oxidation state of the vanadium in the VOx films. In the electrical resistivity measurements, a rectangular slice of the film was placed on the resistivity puck, and four contacts were given using RS component silver paste. Temperature-dependent resistance was measured using the conventional four-probe technique in electrical transport option (ETO) mode of physical property measurement system by applying 10 nA current and 0.5 Hz frequency in the temperature range of 10–300 K.
